storyPrompt: Write a quiet English story about checking a disputed delivery before a public demonstration. Pema is a practical conservator. Cal is an assistant who is allowed to disagree. Eli keeps the public records. The story takes place at the salt archive. The wax packet must remain intact. No character may be physically injured. Keep practical actions precise. Use third-person past tense centred on Pema. Plan six chapters, each targeting 750 words. No earlier book or borrowed fictional world is assumed.

chapters.turn: Eli supplies a duplicate page; the team agrees to continue checking before a demonstration.

chapters.purpose: Pema compares the duplicate with a pencil copy.

chapters.title: Demonstration
chapters.purpose: The team prepares the public demonstration at the salt archive.
chapters.turn: Pema credits Cal for finding the error, without claiming the item was lost.

chapters.purpose: Pema completes the demonstration and files the corrected tide register.
chapters.turn: The intact wax packet is stored securely and the dispute is closed.

texts:
Pema received the sealed wax packet and checked its outer label. The salt archive was open, though there were no visitors at the table. Pema cleared a space before setting anything down. Cal moved the loose tools to a tray and waited for instructions. Neither of them treated a late delivery as proof of a lost object. They checked what they could see and left a blank beside what they could not yet establish.

The work required a little patience. A faded number was difficult to distinguish from a stain, so Pema turned the sheet towards the window rather than writing over it. Cal read the number aloud. They compared their readings, found that they agreed, and entered it only once. The wax packet remained intact on the cleared table throughout the check.

Pema made a short note of the work completed that day. The note separated observation from intention: a task written for tomorrow did not become a task already done. Cal asked whether the uncertainty meant they should abandon the demonstration. Pema said that an unanswered question was a reason to check, rather than a reason to invent an answer. It was an ordinary distinction, but making it aloud helped them continue without blaming anyone.

Pema noticed a red seam but left it unopened. They put the tools back in the tray. Pema recorded that result and closed the current work period. The next planned task remained unwritten in the story. No one had opened a different room, visited another site, or completed the later demonstration in the interval between these actions.
